notes: Nimbus does not accumulate: mean luminance oscillates around 168 over a 72.8 YAVG range with no net drift (-7.6 from 30-100 s, -3.0 from 100-200 s), so any clean run will do and the choice is purely the endpoint match. Six clean runs of 16 s or more; every 0.1 s start in each was scanned, and 175.0-190.0 s wins at +0.01 YAVG end-to-start, sitting inside the 38.2 s run with ~5.8 s of margin either side. The engine renders Nimbus at render_scale=0.50 and upscales, so it is softer than Fractal Tree or Skein — the app's own choice, not a capture fault. A first take was discarded: Uzume was windowed, so the render target was 1920x1018 and the encoder's size assertion would have rejected it.

PASS longest clean run, no gaps or duplicates: 172.5 s (4.2-176.7 s)
notes: Cleanest take of W.3c: one 172.5 s clean run covering all but the first 4.2 s, full render_scale=1.00. Window chosen on Matt's rule that a gallery loop should showcase the preset's responsivity from an early window of playback, not merely seam the tidiest. Frame-to-frame motion (mean abs interframe difference) is front-loaded here — 9-13 between 21 s and 50 s, settling to 4-6 after ~100 s — so every 0.5 s start from the in point was scored on motion first and seam second. 31.5-46.5 s takes motion 9.17 against a 9.30 peak with a -0.28 YAVG endpoint match; a seam-only pick would have sat late in the take at motion 4-6. The ring visibly pulses across the span, which also answers the roster note that Nebula 'should look more activated'.

check: duplicate consecutive frames in the whole file: 45
PASS longest clean run, no gaps or duplicates: 93.2 s (11.0-104.2 s)
notes: Nacre is a full-frame iridescent sheet, and its hue drifts continuously, so the seam risk here is COLOUR, not luma — encode_captures' seam gate only measures YAVG and is blind to it. Scoring on luma alone picked 54.5-69.5 s (best motion variation, ΔY -3.56) but that span runs teal to green: chroma Δ 98.1. Rescoring on UAVG/VAVG gives 84.5-99.5 s at chroma Δ 44.1, consistently yellow-green end to end, keeping motion sd 9.00 against a 11.77 peak. For calibration, raw span drift in the already-published masters: Fractal Tree 0.60, Cymatic 0.98, Murmuration 2.14, Skein 2.61 — and Ferrofluid Ocean 128.43, whose aurora shifts hue with the vocal line and which shipped with Matt's approval. So 44.1 sits well inside precedent and the 0.5 s crossfade absorbs it. Separately, the roster note that Nacre is 'too fast overall' is measurable: mean interframe difference is 137.6 against Nebula's 9.2, and it barely varies (sd 10.6, 7.7% of mean), so the motion does not track the music. Flash safety is not at issue: per-frame luma change is mean 0.20 / max 4.76 on an 8-bit scale, against Ferrofluid Ocean's 0.13 / 2.56.
hold: not web-publishable at 15 s. Nacre is a full-frame high-frequency iridescent field with a mean interframe difference of 137.6 (Nebula: 9.2), so it is close to incompressible. In budget at 12 MB it encodes to SSIM Y 0.476 (WebM) and 0.441 (H.264) — mush, against 0.93 for Ferrofluid Ocean, the hardest preset shipped. Uncapped AV1 at CRF 30 is 299 MB for 15 s and still only SSIM 0.711: 25x the gallery budget for quality below anything published. The H.264 attempt also failed the chroma seam bar at dUV 1.50 against a 0.84 in-loop maximum.
